{"self_assessment": "Impact: I fetched a full 40-domino load for the shared bin early, which kept the whole table supplied so nobody stalled waiting on material. I laid the upper tail from the sketch, and it came out clean to its tip. When the nose joint wasn't catching, I extended the start line from its live end and curved it up to meet the top line. That bridge is what got the run connected, and about 88 of the 93 standing dominoes fell from the start. The leftover pale ones sat in the nose and didn't touch the outline.

Execution: I worked in short, steady stretches on the upper tail, then inspected the nose closely before changing anything. I used a gentle extension in place of a sharp corner, which suits how the dominoes actually pass the fall. Once the run was catching, I stopped adding pieces so the table wouldn't bump each other or break what was working.

Collaboration: I confirmed the plan out loud, told Priya when the upper tail was down, and flagged the nose problem so we could look at it together. I kept clear of the nose once others were checking it, and I backed the hands-off decision in the final minutes.

Leadership: I stayed in step with Priya's plan and committed to the fish early. I took the supply run and the upper tail without being asked twice, and I helped steer the group to leave the finished fish alone before the push. Being willing to step back from a working build was part of getting a clean result.", "my_share_percent": 30}
